message.content:
This is a small handheld vacuum with an electric motor, designed to clean hearing aids. Two headings are candidates: 8508 (vacuum cleaners) and 9021 (parts and accessories of hearing aids).

Heading 8508 covers vacuum cleaners with a self-contained electric motor. Subheading 8508.11 is for motors not exceeding 1,500 W with a dust bag or other receptacle capacity not exceeding 20 L, but it is limited to 8508.11 as a vacuum cleaner with an output of 1,500 W or less. Under the 2022 revision, 8508.11 was restructured. The current layout is:
- 8508.11.00 is for vacuum cleaners with a self-contained electric motor, 1,500 W or less, with a bag or receptacle not over 20 L.
- 8508.19 covers other vacuum cleaners.
- 8508.60 covers other vacuum cleaners.

Heading 9021 covers hearing aids, and 9021.40 covers hearing aids excluding parts and accessories. Accessories are classified under 9021.90. A cleaning vacuum for hearing aids is arguably an accessory, but 9021 is limited to articles that are worn or carried, or implanted in the body, to compensate for a defect or disability. Section XVI Note 1 and Chapter 90 Note 1 would also come into play. A cleaning device is not worn, so it does not fit that wording. Chapter 85 is likely more appropriate, particularly given that heading 8508 describes the device by its function.

The device has a battery, so it is cordless. In the current HTSUS, 8508.11.00 is "Vacuum cleaners, with self-contained electric motor: of a power not exceeding 1,500 W and having a dust bag or other receptacle capacity not exceeding 20 L." The statistical suffix is 8508.11.0000 (the 2022 HTSUS has 8508.11.00 with 00 in the last two digits). The 8508.60 line is "other vacuum cleaners," and 8508.70 is for parts. Since the description states motor power ≤1,500 W and a small collection chamber, 8508.11.0000 fits.
